ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
China's "Tianzhou-1" cargo spacecraft successfully completed the autonomous rapid rendezvous and docking test with the "Tiangong-2" space laboratory. This test reduced the preparation time for China's space rendezvous and docking from two days to 6.5 hours, laying a more solid technical foundation for the subsequent development and construction of China's space station project. The figure is a schematic diagram of the docking process between "Tianzhou" and "Tiangong". It is known that after the successful docking of "Tianzhou-1" and "Tiangong-2", the combined body operates in a circular orbit. After a time $t$, the combined body has rotated through an angle $\theta$ around the Earth. The Earth's radius is $R$, the gravitational acceleration at the Earth's surface is $g$, and the gravitational constant is $G$. The Earth's rotation is not considered.

1. The mass of the Earth $M$
2. The period of motion of the combined system is $T$.
3. The altitude of the circular orbit of the combined body above the ground is $H$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the Earth is located at the center, and a circular orbit is drawn on the outside; the docked spacecraft is located at the upper position of the circular orbit, and the velocity direction v is along the tangential direction of the orbit. The line connecting the spacecraft to the center of the Earth indicates that it undergoes circular motion around the center of the Earth, so the orbital radius is r = R + H. Reasoning: It is known that the combined body turns through an angle θ around the Earth within time t, so the angular velocity ω = θ/t. The period of circular motion T = 2π/ω = 2πt/θ. The gravitational acceleration at the Earth's surface satisfies g = GM/R^2, so the Earth's mass M = gR^2/G. When the combined body undergoes circular orbital motion, universal gravitation provides the centripetal force: GMm/r^2 = mω^2r, so r^3 = GM/ω^2. Substituting M = gR^2/G and ω = θ/t, obtain r^3 = gR^2t^2/θ^2, therefore r = (gR^2t^2/θ^2)^(1/3). The orbital height is H = r - R, so H = (gR^2t^2/θ^2)^(1/3) - R.
